open_points.subject: component-by-component Linux path opening shared by installation and store
open_points.text: “The data directory itself is reached as A17 rule 1 reaches the configuration file, component by component with `O_NOFOLLOW`” conflicts with the module split in which `installation` owns A17, `store` owns A18, and “modules on one line do not know each other.”
open_points.question: Which module owns the shared component-by-component `O_NOFOLLOW`/`O_PATH` path-opening mechanism, and in which dependency direction may both `installation` and `store` use it?
options: `installation` owns it and `store` may depend on `installation`
`store` owns it and `installation` may depend on `store`
a lower shared module owns it and both modules depend on that module
both modules independently implement and own the same mechanism
open_points.default_guess: Introduce a lower shared host-path module used by both `installation` and `store`.

open_points.subject: installation files located inside the store-owned data directory
open_points.text: A17 says “Nothing requires these paths to lie outside the data directory, and nothing checks it,” while State 3 says “only `store` touches the database and the data directory” and assigns configuration and credential-file reads to `installation`.
open_points.question: When the configuration file or a credential file lies inside `data_directory`, may `installation` open it directly, is that placement forbidden, or must access be routed through `store` despite the fixed startup order loading `installation` before opening `store`?
options: make an explicit exception allowing `installation` to open configured files inside the data directory
forbid configuration and credential paths inside the data directory
route such access through `store` and change the dependency/startup order
narrow “only `store` touches the data directory” to store-managed artifacts rather than every path beneath it
open_points.default_guess: Narrow the State 3 boundary to store-managed artifacts and explicitly allow `installation` to read configured files that happen to be beneath the data directory.
